=== HANDOFF #8 — epic e369 (Jira Server/Data Center). READ THIS, THEN #7, THEN #6. ===

WORKTREE /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family, branch jira-family-seam. ALWAYS:
export PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"

*** WHAT CHANGED THIS SESSION: ALL FOUR SHIPPED-CODE DEFECTS ARE CLOSED, J11'S PLAN PASSED AND IS
CLAIMED, AND ITS THIN SLICE IS 3/4 GREEN LIVE. THE OUTBOUND HALF OF THE HEADLINE AC IS STILL
UNPROVEN. ***

CLOSED: 9263 (plan_defect), 21fc, 387d, 7c26 (all preexisting). e369's open children are now
5200 (J11, IN PROGRESS, claimed), b586, cc77, fe15, 6a91.

MERGED THIS SESSION: 1129 1130 1131 1136 (the original stack) + 1150 1151 1152 1153 (follow-ups
the close gate forced) + 1158 1159 1161 1162 (J11's slice). Twelve changes.

*** THE ONE OPEN PROBLEM — READ THE RULED-OUT LIST BEFORE FORMING A HYPOTHESIS ***

`test_a_dc_issue_reaches_the_local_store_inbound` FAILS live. Latest: run 30699907628, job
91368976778. 1 failed, 23 passed. The pass prints:

  RECON: outbound_differ total=1639 create=1639 update=0 delete=0
  RECON: inbound_differ total=0 with_fields=0 with_labels=0 with_comments=0
  filter: 1640 mutations computed, 0 match filter (1 local IDs, 1 target keys)
  RECON: typed_inbound_dispatched count=0 suppressed_pairs=0

The DC issue is created, then a `bootstrap-strict` pass scoped with
`--filter-local-ids jira-<key>` is run, and the local ticket never appears.

ALREADY RULED OUT — do NOT re-test these, each cost a full harness cycle (~8 min + review + merge):
 1. FIXTURE SCOPING. First failure was `fixture 'dc_transport' not found` (ERROR at setup) —
    it was module-local to test_transport.py. MOVED to conftest.py (change 1159). Note
    `pytest --collect-only` does NOT catch this; fixtures resolve at SETUP. Use
    `pytest --fixtures <module>` instead.
 2. THE STORE WAS NOT A GIT REPO. Second failure: `binding-store commit to tickets branch failed
    (CalledProcessError(128, ['git','-C','.../.tickets-tracker','commit',...]))`. 128 = "not a git
    repository". `.tickets-tracker/` IS its own repo on the orphan `tickets` branch and the
    reconciler commits into it directly. Fixed in 1161: the tracker gets its own `git init -b
    tickets`, committed AFTER the scrub; the outer repo gitignores it; BOTH get a local committer
    identity (a CI runner has no global one).
 3. INDEX LAG — **HYPOTHESIS DISPROVEN, and I was wrong to assume it.** I added
    `_wait_until_searchable` (1162), which polls `search_issues` until the key is visible and
    fails loudly naming index lag. The latest run did NOT fail that way, so the poll SUCCEEDED:
    the issue WAS searchable and `inbound_differ` still saw nothing. Index lag is not the cause.
    Keep the helper — it is correct and the pagination cell needs it — but stop attributing this
    failure to it.

FACTS GATHERED, so the next session starts from evidence rather than guesses:
 * The fetcher's inbound JQL is a PAIR (fetcher.py:69-81): `project = <KEY> AND status != "Done"`
   and `project = <KEY> AND status = "Done" ORDER BY updated DESC`. A new Task is not Done, so
   jql_active SHOULD match it. `_validate_project_key` interpolates the key UNQUOTED.
 * `--filter-local-ids` is a POST filter, not a scoping optimisation: "1640 mutations computed,
   0 match filter". The whole store is computed every pass. Isolation still held — 0 applied.
 * outbound_differ computing 1639 creates is EXPECTED and harmless here: the scrub removes every
   binding, so every copied ticket looks new (`outbound_differ.py:518-520` routes jira_key None to
   CREATE). The filter drops them all.

THE PRIME SUSPECT AND THE SAFE EXPERIMENT. It is not established whether the RECON counters are
printed before or after the filter is applied. If AFTER, then `inbound_differ total=0` is telling
us the FILTER removed the inbound create rather than that the differ never made one — and the
whole diagnosis flips. TEST IT WITHOUT MUTATING THE HARNESS: run the same pass as
`--mode dry-run` WITHOUT `--filter-local-ids` and inspect the envelope's `.plan` for an entry with
`direction == "inbound"` and `action == "create"` naming the key. Dry-run writes nothing, so the
1639 outbound creates cannot fire. Do NOT run an unfiltered WRITING pass — bootstrap-strict
(cap=10, mode.py:106) would file 10 production tickets into the harness, and `live` would file all
1639.
Second suspect if that comes back clean: compare against
`test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` in test_reconcile_pass.py, which
does the same inbound round-trip and PASSES. The material differences are (a) it uses the
`rebar_repo` empty store, not a copied one, and (b) it runs UNFILTERED. Diffing those two cells is
probably the shortest path to the answer.

WHAT IS PROVEN GREEN LIVE (all three passed on every run since 1158):
 * `test_the_working_repo_is_isolated_from_this_project` — no remote on BOTH repos (the outer one
   AND the store repo, which is the one that would actually push), REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off, no Cloud
   credential.
 * `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` — 2673 ticket entries extracted into
   `.tickets-tracker/`, count MATCHING `git ls-tree origin/tickets` exactly (a count comparison,
   not a `> 0` floor, so a PARTIAL extraction fails), and zero `.bridge_state*` survivors.
 * `test_the_scrubbed_copy_plans_no_deletions_or_outbound_updates` — zero deletions AND zero
   outbound updates over the real copy, confirming from a live instance the reasoning that an
   outbound UPDATE cannot be emitted without a binding.

J11's PLAN PASSED AFTER 12 ROUNDS and is SIGNED (head_sha 1895c987b8). Finding counts went
6,3,4,3,4,2,3,2,4,1,2,0. Do not reopen settled ACs. The three deepest corrections it produced:
 * `scanned` is `len(curr_snapshot)` — the count of REMOTE Jira issues (`reconcile.py:286`), NOT
   local tickets. So it can never prove the store copy is non-empty. **This also corrects handoff
   #4**, which read an early run's `scanned=0` as "the STORE was EMPTY"; on this code it means the
   HARNESS had no issues. The store-copy AC now counts tickets on the filesystem instead.
 * In DRY-RUN there is no `scanned=` line at all — `persist` is False, so it takes the skip branch
   and prints `invariants: skipped (no-write mode, <N> issues in snapshot)` to STDERR. Only an
   UNFILTERED WRITING pass prints `scanned=` to STDOUT. I got this wrong twice in the plan.
 * Outbound rows 2-13 are all UPDATEs and need a binding the scrub removes, so they share a
   `bound_dc_issue` fixture: create the DC issue, run a writing pass SCOPED with
   `--filter-local-ids jira-<dc_key.lower()>` (computable in advance because
   `_jira_key_to_local_id` is pure, `inbound_translate.py:120-124`), then mutate locally. There is
   NO inbound-only mode — every writing mode also runs the outbound differ — which is why that
   filter is mandatory.

REMAINING J11 WORK: fix the inbound cell, then the outbound round-trip + the `bound_dc_issue`
fixture, then the 28-cell mutation suite per the plan's oracle table, then pagination
(unfiltered DRY-RUN + poll until all seeded keys are searchable), then idempotence.

STANDING RULES — the three that bit hardest this session, added to the ones in #6/#7:
 * A `rebar edit`/`comment` CAN FAIL ON LOCK CONTENTION and the surrounding script still reports
   OK: `flock: could not acquire lock after 60s`. The other session
   (/Users/joeoakhart/rebar-wt-provider-seam) holds the store lock. ALWAYS re-read and compare
   LENGTH after a write; retry on mismatch.
 * THE GITHUB MIRROR LAGS GERRIT. After a submit, `origin/main` may not have the content for a
   minute or two — that is NOT a failed submit. Verify against `git fetch gerrit main` first, and
   wait for the mirror before dispatching a workflow that runs `--ref main`.
 * `pytest --collect-only` PROVES NOTHING ABOUT FIXTURES. They resolve at setup. Use
   `pytest --fixtures <module>`.
 * Don't background a long command with a bare `&` — it escapes harness task tracking and you get
   no completion notification. Use the proper background mechanism.
